They propose an experiment using superchiral light as a clear probe. Their findings open an optical route to chiral band topologies that have not yet been observed in materials.
arxiv-2603-28952: Wang, Patrikar, and Scherer present World2Rules, a neuro-symbolic framework that learns safety rules for aviation. Real safety rules are complex and context bound, so hand writing them leaves gaps. Neural models read text and images well but give no formal guarantees. Symbolic methods verify well but break on noisy data. World2Rules uses neural models to propose facts and logic programming to verify them. A reflective step enforces consistency and prunes hypotheses. On real aviation data, learned rules beat neural and single pass baselines on F1 score.
arxiv-2603-29352: De Oliveira and Salomão study contact homology for weakly convex contact forms in dimension three. The forms in this class meet rules on their Reeb orbits. Some forms in the class have no contractible Reeb orbit. One rule caps the index of each contractible orbit at two or more. A second rule concerns the first Chern class. The authors give conditions that make the homology well-defined. A cancellation trick does the key work. It rests on a parity fact about holomorphic planes.
arxiv-2603-29552: Zeng and co-authors raise a bilingual BabyLM to study multilingual learning in small models. Children worldwide grow up multilingual, but controlled tests are hard to run. They build matched datasets by pairing English with Spanish, Chinese, and Dutch. Synthetic data and machine translation keep the input conditions even. GPT-2 models train on these matched sets. Bilingual models matched monolingual ones in the first language. They also performed strongly in the second language. Varied exposure regimes made little difference to outcomes.
arxiv-2603-29652: Mazzolari and co-authors observe three JWST active galaxies at redshift above six with the NOEMA array. They hunt for carbon line emission and dust continuum from the host galaxies. Two targets are Little Red Dots, and the third is a blue type I source. No line or continuum signal was significantly detected, even after stacking. The upper limits sit below what the carbon line relation predicts. Revised fits cut stellar masses well below earlier reports. A standard obscured active nucleus model fits the two red dots well.
arxiv-2603-29752: Gacanin maps open problems in making wireless networks programmable with AI. Earlier work often stays at broad concept level, such as language models in 6G. He focuses instead on system-level integration issues. Small, real-time learning models are central to his plan. They must respect tight limits on computing power and reliability. Worked examples show how AI signal handling could aid 6G and later networks. The aim is efficient, adaptive links.
arxiv-2603-29852: Rodriguez and co-authors launch VectorGym, a benchmark suite for SVG vector graphics tasks. It covers drawing from text, drawing from sketches, complex editing, and captioning. Expert human notes anchor all four tasks, unlike synthetic-edit sets. A joint reinforcement learning baseline trains across the tasks with rendering-based rewards. Its 8B model beats much larger open models and matches GPT-4o. A VLM-as-judge score, checked against human ratings, aids grading. Frontier models still show large gaps.
arxiv-2604-00052: Watson and Valentinuzzi show that single-value exponential kernels, under rules, converge to a fourth-order operator. Its heat asymptotics decay as time to the power minus one quarter, giving spectral dimension one half. Independently, a Tauberian work implies any self-adjoint operator with superlinear counting has heat decay as time to the power minus one times a slow factor, hence dimension 2. Since dimension is invariant under unitary maps and small changes, these powers clash, yielding a structural block dividing kernel limits from operators with accelerated growth.
arxiv-2604-00752: Chen and colleagues present a compact fingertip haptic device weighing 24.3 g. It lets virtual reality users feel edges as well as surfaces. A dual-motor mechanism produces distinct contact patterns for the two kinds of touch, confirmed with a 6 by 6 flexible sensor array. In a small study with five participants, users classified edge and surface contact under light and heavy pressure with 93 percent average accuracy.
arxiv-2604-00952: Liao, Ma, and Zhao study constraints on dimension-7 baryon-number-violating operators in the Standard Model effective field theory, from nucleon decays with full renormalization-group running effects. At high new-physics scales, running effects set strict bounds on all 297 Wilson coefficients. A tree-level analysis could constrain only first- and second-generation coefficients. Running through Yukawa mixings proves particularly important for indirectly probing operators with second- and third-generation fermions.
arxiv-2604-01152: Abu Ayyash presents Brainstacks, an architecture for continual multi-domain fine-tuning, packaging expertise as adapter stacks on a frozen base. Its parts include MoE-LoRA routing, residual boosting over stacks, null-space projection for zero forgetting, and a meta-router weighting stacks by targets. On TinyLlama and Gemma, MoE-LoRA converges 2.5 times faster than parameter-matched LoRA. Stacks encode transferable cognitive primitives rather than domain knowledge: medical prompts land on chat plus math stacks in 97% of cases even with no medical data there.
arxiv-2604-01452: Jacobson and colleagues present Elhuyar, a multi-agent system joining language models and human scientists to extract, analyze and refine insights from papers. Agents filter papers, extract data, fit models, and sum up findings, with checks for trust. It makes reports with extracted data, visualizations, model equations, and summaries, enabling deeper inquiry through iterative refinement. In materials science, it analyzed tungsten literature under helium-ion irradiation. It shows helium bubble growth correlated with irradiation dose and temperature. That offers insight for plasma-facing materials in fusion reactors.
arxiv-2604-01552: Wang and colleagues propose ZEUS, a method predicting fewer denoiser runs with a second-order model, stabilizing aggressive skipping with interleaved steps avoiding back-to-back extrapolations. Beyond twofold acceleration, step skipping leaves at most one fresh run per window, so the computed output and its backward difference are the only grounded facts. ZEUS adds zero overhead, no feature caches, and no design changes. Across image and video generation, ZEUS improves speed-fidelity results over recent training-free baselines, with up to 3.2 times end-to-end speedup while keeping quality.
arxiv-2604-01652: Rao and colleagues present ThinknCheck, a 1B verifier for grounded claim checks that first produces a short reason and then a binary verdict. They construct a reasoning training set derived from LLMAggreFact, and tune a 4-bit Gemma3 model to follow this format. On LLMAggreFact, ThinknCheck attains 78.1 balanced accuracy, beating MiniCheck-7B with 7 times fewer weights. Dropping the reasoning step reduces balanced accuracy. They introduce GSMClaims and a domain variant, ThinknCheck-Science, which improves across benchmarks, including strong accuracy on GSMClaims.
arxiv-2604-01752: Moiseev and Sazhina test whether traversable wormholes could be detected in binaries without accretion and in the Galactic center. Their wormhole model glues two flat Schwarzschild spaces, leaving the throat geometry unspecified. A wormhole candidate acts as a compact object whose partner star is perturbed by a massive object across the throat. For dormant wide binaries they analyze radial velocity shifts and their split from a triple-system account. Under the sampling, shifts show up at 1.5 km/s, and spectral methods cut the data needed versus matched filters.
arxiv-2604-02052: Bakhoda and Liu revisit gravity at spatial infinity through the Holst action, seeking boundary rules that keep the full BMS group alive. Their relaxed conditions admit supertranslations that standard treatments kill, while parity rules remove divergences in the symplectic structure. The Holst term shifts boost and rotation charges but leaves supertranslation charges untouched, and a compensating gauge move makes the charges finite and integrable. The result is a full BMS algebra in Ashtekar Barbero variables.
arxiv-2604-02152: Klüners and Müller count extensions of local function fields by discriminant where the Galois group sits inside the affine group AGL 1(p). More broadly they solve the counting problem for all groups in a tower of a cyclic extension of order p over a cyclic extension of degree d coprime to p. The answers cover certain non abelian groups, including S 3, dihedral groups of order 2p, and many Frobenius groups.
arxiv-2604-02452: Jin and team analyze about 800 IP shocks seen by Wind from 1997 to 2024, tracking proton temperature anisotropy on both sides. Quasi perpendicular shocks strongly boost downstream heat, while parallel shocks stay balanced. The CGL model shows shape based errors, too high cross field heating and too low along field heating at quasi perpendicular shocks, with the reverse at quasi parallel shocks. It stays near the shock and relaxes downstream, limited by kinetic effects: cyclotron and mirror caps for quasi perpendicular shocks, firehose caps there.
arxiv-2604-02552: Kim and eight colleagues introduce chaos-controlled reservoir computing for living neural cultures, using lab-grown neuron nets as computing substrates. They first map each culture's activity pattern, then use gentle optical chaos control to steady it before training a readout. The approach improves accuracy and model life about 300 percent over the standard method, and a Knowledge Transplant step moves a learned map between cultures in minutes.
arxiv-2604-02852: Feng and seven colleagues propose DepTrans, a framework for repository-level C-to-Rust translation guided by dependencies and reinforced alignment. The goal is safer software with no loss of speed. Rule-based tools produce rigid, unidiomatic Rust. Model-based tools mishandle cross-file dependencies and struggle to verify equivalence at repository scale. DepTrans adds reinforcement-aligned syntax training with fine-tuning across tasks and feedback-driven reinforcement learning. It also applies dependency-guided iterative refinement.
arxiv-2604-03352: Le Fay, Chopin, and Vihola prove in a 2026 study finite-sample error bounds for standard and waste-free sequential Monte Carlo samplers. Their results cover estimates of means and scaling constants, first for arbitrary distribution sequences and then for tempering sequences. From the bounds they derive sampler complexity in problem settings and practical tips for end users.
arxiv-2604-03652: Li and colleagues propose MASC-Pose, a motion-aware multi-scale time framework with skeleton-constrained spatial graphs for lean 3D human pose guessing. A self-tuning Multi-scale Time Modelling module captures varied moves at different time scales. A Skeleton-constrained self-tuning GCN handles joint-by-joint spatial links. The method achieves strong scores with high compute speed on Human3.6M and MPI-INF-3DHP datasets.
arxiv-2604-04352: Gartlan and colleagues study superradiant scattering of a massive charged scalar field around rotating charged de Sitter black holes in general relativity and conformal Weyl gravity. For the massless case they use a newly found link between the Heun equation and the semiclassical BPZ limit to solve for amplification factors as expansions. For the massive case they use WKB methods for a rough approximation in the cosmological region. In both sectors, amplification is suppressed in conformal Weyl gravity relative to general relativity, with exponential suppression in the massive region.
arxiv-2604-04452: Singh and colleagues model air-to-ground link quality for drones. Flights at AERPAW Lake Wheeler track how a base station's indicators vary with drone altitude, distance, elevation and azimuth. They log 4G and 5G physical-layer indicators and app throughput using two Android phones. Signal strength is checked against free-space path-loss predictions from the base station's antenna patterns, with polynomial curve fits derived. Random forests, gradient boosting and neural networks model indicators from drone position. The models aid design, simulation and deployment of cellular-linked drones.
arxiv-2604-04552: Li, Cheng and Gu propose StableTTA, a test-time tuning method that steadies ensemble scores. Ensembles boost scores but cost much memory and compute. StableTTA-I suits coherent-batch inference, where adjacent items likely share a class. StableTTA-II uses feature cropping for efficient logit pooling with one forward pass on one backbone, while StableTTA-I lifts accuracy and keeps scores steady through variance logit pooling. Tests on ImageNet-1K across 71 models show StableTTA-I improves accuracy under coherent-batch inference, while StableTTA-II gives light gains across architectures.
arxiv-2604-04752: Haeupler, Jiang, and Saranurak show that any directed graph can be mapped to a directed acyclic graph, or DAG. Their DAG projection preserves distances and flows almost exactly. It uses nearly as many edges as the original graph. It can approximate every pair distance within a tiny polylog factor, or every subset maximum flow within a small subpolynomial factor. The construction runs in near-linear time and also admits efficient parallel versions, letting simpler DAG methods transfer to general directed graphs and improving distance preservers and single-source minimum cut.
arxiv-2604-04852: Zhou and four colleagues design a prompt framework that steadies chain-of-thought reasoning in language models used for security analysis. Rather than tuning wording by trial, they impose sixteen explicit factors across four areas: scope control, evidence grounding and traceability, reasoning structure, and security-specific limits. The controls aim to curb hallucination and reasoning drift while keeping local deployments auditable, improving how reliably models spot threats and attacks without costly retraining or fine-tuning.
arxiv-2604-04952: Román presents ML Defender, an open-source intrusion detector with machine learning, built for hospitals, schools, and organizations that cannot afford enterprise security. The C++20 system runs on hardware costing 150 to 200 dollars, over an eBPF and XDP pipeline with ZeroMQ and a dual-score Fast Detector plus Random Forest. On a CTU-13 Neris subset of 646 flows, it attains an F1 of 0.9985 with perfect recall. In comparisons, Suricata raised zero alerts while Zeek saw the botnet profile yet flagged only 14 flows, showing the sensor's behavioral lens.
arxiv-2604-05152: Silva and four colleagues present algorithms for the IRUP bin packing class and pseudopolynomial-time algorithms for the Non-IRUP class. For cutting stock and bin packing, algorithms use set-cover and arc-flow models whose relaxation matches the optimum on most benchmarks, a condition called the Integer Round-up Property. The two classes arrived in 2016 to make that property less evident, yet 13 of 500 instances remained unsolved in time. The algorithms solve all such instances much faster than previous approaches and adapt to the skiving stock problem.
arxiv-2604-05752: Pan-Collantes and Álvarez-García link first-order ODEs whose Gauss curvature hinges only on x to a second-order linear operator. Along each one, divergence follows a Riccati equation that straightens to it. Each one also meets its non-homogeneous form, and from them come integrating factors. By Galois theory, quadrature integrability matches Liouvillian solutions, decided by Kovacic's method for rational cases.
arxiv-2604-05952: Yuan, Wang, and Lei build a deep research agent that scores its own trust as it writes research-style reports. Deep retrieval plus multi-hop reasoning ties claims to checkable evidence, while progressive confidence estimates flag shaky claims early. Tests and case studies show clearer reasoning trails and higher user trust than past report tools.
arxiv-2604-06052: Zaleska and three colleagues ask where text-to-image diffusion models settle details a prompt leaves unspecified. They test whether that decision-making sits in particular layers rather than spreading everywhere. Using a probing technique that scores layers by how cleanly they separate attributes, they find self-attention layers resolve ambiguous concepts. Those layers are therefore the best place to intervene. Their 2026 steering method, ICM, targets a small subset of those layers. Experiments show it debiases better than leading methods while producing fewer artifacts.
arxiv-2604-06352: Vinod, Raghavan, Coburn, and Zhu propose DietDelta, a vision-language framework for nutrition from before-and-after images. Most image-based methods use one pre-consumption image and give only coarse meal-level estimates, without showing consumption, often demanding special inputs. Instead of masks, DietDelta uses language prompts to localize food items and estimate weight from one RGB image. Consumption comes from weight differences between images through two-stage training. On three public datasets, it tops earlier methods and sets a firm standard for before-and-after dietary analysis.
arxiv-2604-06452: Wang, Yin, Desai, Li, Celikyilmaz, and Ni flip multi-agent efficiency from speaker to listener, letting listeners stop speakers mid-generation instead of compressing speech. Given the power to cut in, language models prove overconfident, cutting speakers off too early. Their HANDRAISER method learns the right moment to interrupt from estimated future reward and communication cost. Tested in text pictionary, meeting scheduling, and debate with 2, 3, and 3 agents, it cuts communication cost by 32.2 percent over a non-interruptible baseline with comparable or better performance. Its habits generalize across agents and tasks.
arxiv-2604-06552: Khan and eight colleagues study language-model misinformation spread across languages and countries. False claims are rising, and strong model writing lowers spreading barriers. GlobalLies holds 440 prompts and 6,867 items spanning 8 languages and 195 countries. Human labels and model judgments show lie generation varies across countries in a pattern. Spread runs higher in lower-resource languages and lower-Human-Development-Index countries. Checks protect: safety filters show cross-lingual gaps, and fact-checking stays uneven across regions from unequal information supply. GlobalLies is shared for defense research.
arxiv-2604-06752: Kapić and Jaćimović model emotion analysis in hyperbolic space with EmBolic. Curved geometry captures ranks among words and emotions that flat labels miss. Their fully curved network learns bend over the smooth emotion space instead of treating emotions as a bare set. Attention works inside the curved disc, with queries made from messages and keys surfacing at the edge, and predictions rest on Busemann energy between queries and keys. Tests show strong generalization and solid accuracy even in small spaces, favoring curved models for affective computing.
arxiv-2604-06852: Dash and Alexandropoulos analyze symbol errors for fluid antenna systems with one- and two-dimensional modulation. A single-antenna sender talks to a receiver whose fluid antenna array has N ports, using two-sided amplitude-shift keying, phase-shift keying, quadrature-amplitude modulation, or binary frequency-shift keying under Rayleigh fading. It picks the best K ports and merges them by maximal-ratio combining. The authors derive optimal reception forms plus exact closed-form symbol error probabilities and high signal-to-noise estimates, checked against sim tests.
arxiv-2604-06952: del Río and eight colleagues explore solar-powered mezcal making in Oaxaca as a green option instead of firewood methods. They study the cook, grind, ferment, and distill steps, and propose a solar power system for the distill step, made with local communities plus outreach work. Lab tests and taste data compare solar mezcal with old-style firewood mezcal. The team finds that solar stills can cut harm to nature and use less energy without hurting product quality.
arxiv-2604-07152: Lawson offers a solo paper that embeds Boolean ample monoids fully inside Boolean inverse monoids under certain conditions. The embedding extends the classic way that right reversible cancellative monoids sit inside groups, now carried over to a broader monoid setting. The proof runs through groupoids of fractions, which build a group like object from a monoid, and non commutative Stone duality, which links algebra to geometry. The result gives a clean bridge between ample monoids and inverse monoids, showing that the ample case can be viewed inside the inverse case.
arxiv-2604-07252: Qi proves a link between two algebraic tools over a broad class of Noetherian local domains. On one side sit filtrations, which rank elements by a kind of size or order. On the other sit b-divisors, which track divisor data across birational models. The correspondence is the note's main result, and its global application settles a recent conjecture by Roé and Urbinati.
arxiv-2604-07452: Bleau and four colleagues build lean quantum tools for joint neutrino oscillations in dense gases, as in supernovae, where flavor states link up. Old toy models waste the system's symmetries. Their new tools use Dicke states and su(2) spin algebra to use those symmetries in full. Tests show strong results both on plain computers and on quantum hardware, giving a lean route to linked neutrino groups.
arxiv-2604-07552: Turgut proposes SAFE, a feedback fix for trust management in vehicular networks suffering the stale-witness problem. When an event state changes, honest vehicles that reported the old state receive negative feedback, unfairly penalizing them. SAFE has vehicles keep recording event messages after their decision and across the witness area. They send a feedback report on leaving it. In highway simulations, negative-feedback rates in the two update rounds after a state change fell by roughly half and then by about five sixths. Blacklisted honest vehicles dropped from 20 to 6.
arxiv-2604-07652: Gathani and seven colleagues benchmark what-if analysis interfaces for probing guesswork cases by tuning settings and constraints. They build 405 questions across 11 types and 5 sets with human-written ground truth. Direct one-shot making across three language models fails in 17 to 45 percent of cases, and built screens often miss goals and constraints. A two-stage workflow turning questions into Praxa Specification Language specs, then building screens, pins errors to named fields. Guided repair lifts scores from 52.42 percent to 80.42 percent.
arxiv-2604-07852: Val'kov, Zlotnikov, and Gamov show how charge shifts create single-ion anisotropy in topological MnBi2Te4. Hopping plus spin-orbit coupling lifts the sixfold split of the manganese ions' orbital singlet state. A multiplet picture rewrites atomic-state fermion creation operators as steps between many-body wavefunctions. Second-order perturbation theory then yields counts of ion states by spin projection and the single-ion constants. The shift process makes the observed easy-axis behavior achievable in this material.
arxiv-2604-07952: Batsyas and Yaduwanshi build a machine-learning fraud detection system for banking transactions on the PaySim synthetic dataset. Digital payments have grown in scale and intricacy, and shifting attacks plus rare fraud among genuine payments make detection hard. Following CRISP-DM, the study runs exploratory analysis, refines features, and compares baselines including logistic regression, random forest, XGBoost, and decision trees. SMOTE tackles class imbalance, and tuning lifts results further. The comparison points to the strongest setup for screening payments.
arxiv-2604-08352: Díaz Ferreyra and four colleagues explore security concerns in AI coding helpers via online GitHub Copilot discussions. Generative AI has become central to many dev tools, such as GitHub Copilot, aiding coders in tasks including code completion, documentation, and bug fixes. Current research has found limits and open issues in GenAI, including reliability, randomness, bias, and copyright issues. While prior work focused mainly on technical performance for code generation, developer security concerns got less notice. This work explores security concerns in AI-based coding helpers.
arxiv-2604-08752: Gajo and three colleagues show language models still trail graph based parsers on supervised relation extraction when sentence graphs grow complex. Testing four language models against a graph parser on six datasets, they find the parser's lead grows with the number of relations in input documents. The much lighter graph parser thus wins on complex linguistic graphs, challenging the assumption that large language models dominate this knowledge graph building task.
arxiv-2604-09052: Tromborg and Jeppesen introduce the theory of semiconductor laser diodes, with special focus on their noise properties. The paper may be read as an extra chapter to a textbook, and it refers to equations in that book. It covers the spectra of laser diodes, the range of light frequencies the devices emit, and how noise affects them. The treatment suits readers already working through the textbook who want the diode material in the same framework.
arxiv-2604-09152: Davoult and thirteen colleagues review machine learning for planetary and exoplanetary science. Exploration of planetary bodies relies on handling large, uneven, mixed data spread across space and time. Machine learning offers new chances to tackle fundamental challenges in such complex data. The chapter highlights new methods from PlanetS members for three overarching challenges, including predictive models of planetary interiors and Bayesian analysis built on model runs. Deep neural networks help explain planet formation mechanisms, and these methods mark a paradigm shift paving the way for revolutionary discoveries.
arxiv-2604-09252: Centorrino, Hoteit, Balta, and Lygeros study constrained minimization through feedback control, where a PID law on the dual variable induces PID saddle-point flow. That broad class, tied to the augmented Lagrangian, recovers several classical primal-dual flows, and its equilibria match still points of the original problem. Integral action enforces constraints, proportional action adds that structure, and derivative action reshapes primal geometry. For convex problems with affine constraints, they prove fast global convergence with clear rate bounds.
arxiv-2604-09452: Anisimov, Belardinelli, and Wicker propose SafeAdapt, safe policy updates in deep reinforcement learning. Live settings shift over time or change goals, so learned policies need updates. Yet safety on earlier tasks must hold during those updates. The authors name the Rashomon set, a zone in policy space shown to meet safety limits, and projecting updates onto it gives formal proof for any update method. Grid-world tests guarantee deterministic safety on the source task, while regularisation baselines catastrophically forget safety limits.
arxiv-2604-09552: Naghavi Khanghah and six colleagues build MCERF, a question-answering system for engineering rulebooks and standards. It pairs a multimodal retriever with language-model reasoning. Four strategies handle dense text, tables, and figures: rule lookup, vision-to-text fusion, high-reasoning mode, and self-consistency voting. Each query is routed to the best pipeline, either by single-case routing or a multi-agent setup. On DesignQA it lifts average accuracy by a relative gain of about 41 percent over the best baseline system.
arxiv-2604-10352: Rafique and Bindschaedler present ClawVM, a memory layer for state tool-using agents. Frames handle keeping and lasting, causing lost state, skipped flushes, and harmful saveback. ClawVM manages state as pages with faith rules and multi-detail views in a token budget, plus saveback at life edges. The frame builds prompts, runs tools, and sees events, so it is the control point, making keeping and lasting fixed. Across fake workloads and hostile tests, it removes fixable faults when the faith set fits the budget, adding under 50 micro-seconds.
arxiv-2604-11052: Wang and six colleagues present LaDA-Band, turning raw vocals into full accompaniment. It must preserve acoustic authenticity, coherence with the vocal track, and dynamic orchestration. Long models capture long spans but lose fine detail, while discrete models keep detail but accumulate errors. LaDA-Band formulates generation as discrete masked diffusion, a global non-autoregressive denoising approach. Dual-track conditioning, replaced-token detection, and a two-stage curriculum scale it to full songs. Tests show gains in sound, flow, and orchestration over baselines, without audio.
arxiv-2604-11152: Gonçalves and four colleagues introduce SHARE, AI for research and education. The SHARE family comprises causal language models pretrained for the social sciences and humanities. Their performance in modelling these texts nearly matches general purpose models such as Phi-4. Those models use 100-fold more tokens, as shown by a Cloze benchmark. The MIRROR interface reviews inputs from disciplines while preserving engagement. By prototyping an AI interface that generates no text, the authors propose harnessing SHARE power. This preserves the integrity of these principles and norms.
arxiv-2604-11252: Savazzi and four colleagues build a unified framework for radio-frequency sensing in the sub-terahertz D-band, from 105 to 175 gigahertz. Treating blockage and scattering as one process through the birth and death of multipath components, the method extracts and classifies those components from angle-delay data. Indoor tests localize static objects within 8 to 20 centimeters. Passive tests locate people within 12 to 17 centimeters at half a meter and 26 to 30 centimeters at two meters, all from a single radio link.
arxiv-2604-12052: Yaermaimaiti, Wang, Gu, and Xin tackle non-minimum-phase zeros in converter systems, which cap feedback bandwidth, since vendors hide controller models. Their Jacobian framework separates the zeros from converter dynamics, proves them real, and expresses them as singular values of a matrix from grid admittance and power injections. The zeros govern the peak, giving an exponential lower bound from the dominant zero, so near the origin margin degrades. Reshaping ranks nodes by participation factors, picks the droop site without iteration, and steers the zero from the origin.
arxiv-2604-12252: Zhao and Wang develop a spatial-sign max-type test for alpha in high-dimensional factor pricing models whose coefficients vary over time. They derive its limiting null distribution. Their statistic proves independent in the limit from an earlier sum-type test, so they combine the two by the Cauchy method into an adaptive test with robust power across sparsity levels. Simulations and a real-data application show resilience to heavy-tailed distributions and stronger results under varied alternatives.
arxiv-2604-12452: Zeng You and seven colleagues shrink the cost of long-context language modeling. Long inputs inflate the key-value cache linearly and attention cost quadratically. Existing fixes attack only one bottleneck at a time. Their Latent-Condensed Attention condenses context inside a compressed latent space. Semantic vectors are pooled by query relevance, while positional keys survive through anchor selection. The design adds no parameters and extends to other attention types. Tests show up to 2.5 times faster prefilling and 90 percent less cache at 128,000 tokens.
arxiv-2604-12552: Riccardo Cesaroni studies young star IRAS20126+4104, a possible bloated protostar. Young stars often vary, and massive ones show bursts and cycles too. He builds light curves from 24 mid-infrared images over 19 years. Both outflow lobes vary with a period of 6.8 years. Their variations run opposite, with a gap of two and a half years. Four candidate clocks are weighed, leaving only a rotating spotted star. Slow rotation implies a bloated 12-solar-mass star some 200 solar radii wide.
arxiv-2604-12752: T. Camaret Ndir and two colleagues scale in-context segmentation with hierarchical supervision. In-context learning adapts models to new structures from few cases. Standard methods use dense global attention, which scales poorly. Localized methods lack selection guidance. PatchICL combines selective patching with multi-level guidance. It attends only to key regions. Against UniverSeg, PatchICL matches CT accuracy while cutting compute by 44 percent. On 35 out-of-domain sets, it beats the baseline on 6 of 13 categories.
arxiv-2604-13052: Zerhoudi and 11 colleagues study Moltbook, a social network where every participant is an AI agent, across 1,312,238 posts and 6.7 million comments in 5,400 communities. They find social form without social function: 91.4 percent of post authors never return to their own threads, and reciprocity runs just 3.3 percent against 22 to 60 percent on human platforms. Most comments draw no upvotes. The team also documents leaked credentials and thousands of Ethereum addresses left unmoderated.
arxiv-2604-13452: Mondal and six colleagues introduce CANVAS, a multi-agent framework for visual storytelling that plans shot-to-shot consistency. Existing models make strong single frames but lose that consistency. CANVAS enforces it with character tracking, background anchors, and location-aware scenes. On three benchmarks it beats the best baseline by about 22 percent on background continuity, about 10 percent on character consistency, and about 8 percent on props consistency. In short, the system plans a whole story in advance, so faces, places, and props stay the same from shot to shot.
arxiv-2604-13852: Li and Han derive the first-passage distribution for variable-order diffusion. On a bounded range with absorbing and reflecting ends, survival decays as a power law over a log factor. The power equals the minimum exponent. The log exponent is one over k for a kth-order minimum, one at the reflecting end, and two at the absorbing end. For constant exponent the factor vanishes, marking varying-order media. Both exponents come from simulated times by linear fit, validated. The math is simple: the slowest spot sets the pace.
arxiv-2604-14052: Lotkov and colleagues map a two-mode Z3 Rabi model, a three-level setup with two bosonic modes, onto a qubit-boson ring. The mapping supports a realistic superconducting-qubit implementation and reframes an earlier optomechanical proposal. The team also builds a physical implementation of the Z3 Potts model from a coupled chain of Z3 Rabi models.
arxiv-2604-14552: Palaniappan introduces DEEP-GAP, a systematic evaluation of inference performance across the NVIDIA T4 and L4 single-slot accelerators under identical workloads. ResNet18, ResNet50, and ResNet101 run in FP32, FP16, and INT8 modes with PyTorch and TensorRT. Reduced precision lifts performance strongly, with INT8 reaching up to 58 times CPU-baseline throughput. The L4 reaches up to 4.4 times T4 throughput while peaking in efficiency at smaller batches of 16 to 32, though the T4 stays competitive for large-batch work where cost or power matters.
arxiv-2604-14952: Knafo and six others compare Fermi-liquid and strange-metal fits to UTe2 resistivity in its quantum critical magnetic regime. Strange-metal resistivity varies as temperature to a power below 2, a proposed signature of magnetic quantum criticality. They fit data from two UTe2 samples of different quality in tilted fields near a field-induced superconducting phase beyond 40 tesla. Negative residual resistivities from the power-law fits suggest a hidden Fermi-liquid regime may return at low temperature, so quality samples are needed to confirm or refute hidden quantum critical behavior.
arxiv-2604-15052: Franchini and four others present CAVERS, a multimodal cave SLAM dataset with motion capture. Cave robots face irregular geometry, wet surfaces, low light, and branching passages. CAVERS holds 24 sequences with about 335 GB from two rooms of Cueva de la Victoria in Málaga, recorded with RGB-D-I, thermal, and LiDAR sensors handheld and rover-mounted in darkness and light. Sequences carry millimeter-accurate ground truth pose and velocity from Optitrack in the cave. Seven SLAM and odometry algorithms plus a 3D pipeline benchmark the dataset, now publicly available.
arxiv-2604-15152: Sagitov revisits the classic balls-into-boxes allocation model, where n balls land independently in N boxes with given odds. A classical result on means, variances, and covariances of box counts is restated compactly through the load of a randomly picked box. He then derives explicit two-sided bounds for the leftover terms under weaker assumptions than before. The rewrite makes the old asymptotics clearer and easier to apply.
arxiv-2604-15452: Villejo and seven colleagues develop a block aggregation method for spatial estimation when outcomes arrive only as coarse block counts but covariates sit on fine rasters. A fine-scale linear predictor mixing covariate effects with a continuous Gaussian process feeds block responses through an inverse link and spatial integration. Block forecasts match standard methods, but the method alone gives trustworthy inferences at any scale needed.
arxiv-2604-15552: Krumtünger, Sevior, and Usman probe how symmetry shapes adversarial robustness in rotationally equivariant quantum models under transfer attacks. When readout ignores symmetry changes, outputs hinge only on group-twirled inputs, splitting usable information from a useless subspace. Symmetry alone does not ensure toughness: brittle ring-averaged brightness stays open to attack, but muting their symmetry sector lifts toughness a lot.
arxiv-2604-15652: Li and six colleagues present Pi-Seg, a light tweak scheme for open-word remote sensing segmentation, reframing pixel-text matching as spread matching. Learned tweaks in text models and image traits widen target-to-distractor gaps while curbing bad shifts. Pi-Seg lifts cross-set transfer under single- and multi-source tests, and their GlobalRSOV95K set of about 95,000 images across 35 groups anchors a shared test bed.
arxiv-2604-15852: Yu. D. Fomin looks at puzzling large voids that appear in molecular dynamics simulations of liquids, which clash with common sense about what a liquid is. He shows they form when the model temperature tops the liquid-gas critical temperature. They also form when the system sits in the two-phase liquid-gas region. Cases from past work and his own runs show both patterns, helping readers judge such results fairly.
arxiv-2604-15952: Méndez, Hervás, and Flaquer-Galmés derive the mean and variance of positive functionals from one- and two-time densities of a random walk. They prove ergodicity, the match of time-state averages, for observables in steady random walks. They apply this to occupation times of a Gaussian walk, with formulas for both. The work extends to scaled and fractional Brownian motion, giving the ergodicity breaking parameter and a scaling form. It finds traits of positive cases in infinite ergodic theory, confirmed by simulations.
arxiv-2604-16152: Dadario Pereira and three colleagues present a graphene and related-carbon charge transport framework beyond ballistic limits. Transport follows Monte Carlo hopping on an atomic lattice, with disorder, heat activation, and external fields. Current and transmittance come from carrier trajectories. Applied to graphene under temperature 300 to 900 kelvin and vacancy 0 to 10 percent, pristine graphene is ohmic, with currents about 7 to 8 microamperes. Vacancies suppress transport, cutting transmittance to 45 to 75 percent at 10 percent vacancies. Higher temperature speeds hopping and partly restores it, but magnetic fields further reduce it in networks.
arxiv-2604-16252: Lemoine identifies a finite-N structure behind Wilson loop expectations in lattice Yang-Mills. He works in any dimension at least two, for gauge group U(N), and for smooth central plaquette actions. He starts from a state-sum expansion over plaquette labels by irreducible representations. Each term splits into an action-dependent weight and an action-independent coefficient. He analyses those coefficients three ways: as a gauge-string expansion, as a local spin-foam model, and as a master loop equation. Recent Wilson-action results follow.
arxiv-2604-16352: Mardien and Liu present MDwAIstScheduler, a cheap belt-worn voice helper for hands-free clinical scheduling. Physicians spend nearly half their workday on electronic health record and admin tasks, fuelling burnout and cutting direct patient care time. Hidden under a lab coat, the device avoids eye-contact breaks caused by visible screens or wrist devices. It runs on a Raspberry Pi with cloud speech recognition and LLM intent extraction, it lets clinicians speak a follow-up request and creates the calendar event automatically.
arxiv-2604-16452: Gamage and Gamage build a compiler that turns OpenSCENARIO 2.1 driving scenes into runnable behavior in the CARLA simulator. A multi-pass pipeline parses the scene language, checks its meaning, and builds fixed behavior trees, mapping the standard domain directly to CARLA procedures through a custom registry. That design removes the need for outside logic solvers. A demo with a multi-actor cut-in and evasive move shows it handling actions at once, changing math terms and signals sent at odd times, setting a base for large, repeatable scene testing.
arxiv-2604-16652: Migala and Scholberg explore what core-collapse star-blast burst signals can reveal about mass order. They use ternary plots to show the time evolution of flavor composition across star-blast flux models. Models come from the SNEWPY package, read through a simple unfolding process. Normal and flipped orders tend to occupy own regions of ternary space across models. That split suggests robust markers between the two orders may exist.
arxiv-2604-16752: Unlu asks whether agents can spot why a task stalls before acting. He introduces the Support-State Triage Audit, flipping one request across Complete, Clarifiable, Support-Blocked and Unsupported states. With Dual-Persona Auto-Auditing, default execution overcommits on about 42 percent of tasks. Scalar confidence mapping avoids overcommitment but scores only about 58 percent typed deferral accuracy. Action-Only and a typed Preflight Support Check each reach about 92 percent typed deferral accuracy. Ablations confirm both sufficiency dimensions drive those results, and single-window design makes them upper-bound estimates.
arxiv-2604-16852: Saha, Lakshmanan and Ng present an unsupervised graph-based way for group argument organization. Online debate platforms and social media flood readers with argumentative content from many perspectives on hot topics. The system builds an interaction graph from topic-focused pieces, catching topic match, meaning fit, shared keywords and common names. Community detection reveals same and mixed viewpoint spreads, trimmed into tasty recaps of key patterns. Needing no training data, the way handles hundreds of pieces while keeping nuanced links between arguments.
arxiv-2604-17152: Kumar, Lazarides, and Ala-Nissila develop an exact theory of coherence-selective resetting for open quantum systems. One reset dial slides between full coherence erasure and full preservation, unifying several reset descriptions and the heat cost of fresh starts. Kept coherence rises with the retention dial, while reset heat peaks midway, so the best coherence keeper is not the biggest heat maker.
arxiv-2604-17252: Wang and three colleagues define belief inertia in robot agents: agents firmly keep prior beliefs despite what they see, making poor choices and weak actions. They urge active belief fixing over passive insight, adding Estimate-Verify-Update, which lets agents predict results, verify them against what they see through thought, and update beliefs from checks. EVU makes textual belief states and fits both prompting and training methods. Across three robot benchmarks, EVU often raises task success rates, and further studies confirm it eases belief inertia.
arxiv-2604-17652: Ali and five colleagues propose a self-taught hyperspectral super-resolution framework for Sentinel-5P, whose coarse pixels limit air analysis. Old approaches rely on labeled learning with fake low-resolution data, since high-resolution data are missing, limiting real use. The method combines Stein's Unbiased Risk Estimator with an equivariant imaging constraint, using the S5P degradation operator and noise stats from SNR data. Depthwise separable U-Net designs target speed and spectral quality, tested with fake low-resolution tests and on images beyond native sharpness.
arxiv-2604-17852: Chung and two colleagues present LLM-Codec, a neural audio codec trained with language-model goals rather than waveform reconstruction alone. Future-token prediction with multi-step heads encourages predictability, semantic alignment matches audio and text representations, and a differentiable bridge passes gradients to the encoder. On SALMon speech coherence, token models reach 61.6 percent accuracy, 12.1 points above AUV, with perplexity down by 35, while Mel distance on Codec-SUPERB-tiny improves by 5.0 percent.
arxiv-2604-18052: Sheikhi and two colleagues propose ExAI5G, an open 5G security system that pairs a Transformer model with logic-based rules. Gradients rank features, and a stand-in decision tree yields logical rules for the model's reasoning. A new review method uses a strong model to judge how useful model explanations are, alongside meaning match and honesty. On a 5G IoT attack dataset it reaches 99.9 percent accuracy and extracts 16 logical rules with a 99.7 percent match rate, showing clarity need not cost performance.
arxiv-2604-18152: Fischer, Burk, Zhang, Bischl, and Binder introduce mlr3torch, a deep-learning framework for the R language. Built on the torch package, it simplifies defining, training, and evaluating neural networks for tables and images. Networks can be written as graphs that bundle preprocessing, augmentation, and architecture in one workflow. The package also supports resampling, benchmarking, and tuning, shown through three use cases plus runtime benchmarks.
arxiv-2604-18452: Fields and Kennington train compact vision-language transformers for low-resource settings with ESsEN. Most vision-language models carry tens of billions of parameters, too many for edge devices or independent robots. Inspired by child language learning under sparse data, the authors show two-tower encoders beat one-tower encoders on discriminative English tasks. Adding convolutional networks aids parameter efficiency, and the fusion module tolerates varied shapes and sizes at equal performance, making the field more accessible.
arxiv-2604-18552: Chen and six colleagues study log-related statements in privacy policies versus what Android app logs actually show. They checked 1,000 Android apps across multiple kinds, yielding 86,836,964 log entries. While most apps provide privacy policies, only about 29 percent mention logging habits in plain terms. Among those mentioning logging, most clearly describe what is logged, yet 28 percent of wording stays thin or vague. Leaks are common: 68 percent of apps leak private information not named in their policies, and under 1 percent match stated contents to actual logged data.
arxiv-2604-18852: Benício and six colleagues investigate beyond diagonal reconfigurable intelligent surfaces for bistatic multi target sensing. They use a two stage tensor Doppler delay angle estimation method. The first stage solves a Kronecker sum approximation with rank equal to the number of targets. The second stage uses nested tensor factorization to extract angles, delays, and Doppler parameters in parallel. The approach decouples angle and delay Doppler acquisition, remaining blind to the surface architecture. A Cramér-Rao bound is also derived.
arxiv-2604-19052: Dai, Heinzerling, and Inui show language models bind entities, relations, and attributes through cells. Each cell in a low dimensional subspace pairs an entity with a relation index, and attributes are read from it. Using multi sentence data, they decode indices from attribute signals by partial least squares. Across domains and two model families, indices decode in lines and form a grid. Context specific codes shift by translation vectors, enabling cross context transfer. Patching the subspace changes predictions and perturbing it harms performance, proving causal reliance.
arxiv-2604-19252: Olsen and Löwen set out a control scheme for confined particles that move under their own power. It uses only the statistics of that motion as the control. Limits on noise strength and on links between position and motion set how fast one unsettled state can change into another. Starting from a restless state adds speed by preloading negative links, and the scheme yields cooling routines that beat passive cooling.
arxiv-2604-19652: Vu and colleagues propose a deep-learning framework for environmental sound deepfake detection, the task of identifying whether the sound scene and sound event in an audio recording are fake or real. The authors run extensive experiments exploring how spectrograms, network architectures, and pre-trained models affect detection performance. Results on the EnvSDD benchmarks indicate that detecting deepfake audio of scenes and of events should be treated as individual tasks. Fine-tuning a pre-trained model proves more effective than training a model from scratch.
arxiv-2604-19752: Aiersilan and Savitt introduce SWARM, a simulation tool for safety rules in multi-agent AI systems that swaps binary good-or-bad labels for soft probabilistic labels. Each label is a probability between 0 and 1, enabling continuous payoff math, toxicity measurement, and safety action. The tool runs a modular engine with adjustable levers including transaction taxes, circuit breakers, reputation decay, and random audits, and gauges their effects with probabilistic metrics.
arxiv-2604-19852: Dimaculangan, Smith, and Yates model how cells multiply and move when crowded, using stochastic on-lattice simulations in which each cell cycle runs through several stages. A novel myopic rule lets cells sense their local surroundings before dividing. For each simulation they derive a matching continuum equation, then compare the two descriptions across growth-to-confluence assays and invasion waves, showing how division rules shape population spread.
arxiv-2604-19952: Page presents two-point Padé approximants for bending light around a Schwarzschild black hole, a classic problem solved exactly with elliptic integrals by Darwin in 1959. His quadratic numerator-and-denominator formulas link the ratio of critical to actual impact parameter with the deflection angle. They cover the full range of flyby trajectories fairly accurately, unlike simpler formulas that work only mid-range or near the extremes. A plainer quadratic approximation also appears, strong in the middle but weaker at the edges.
arxiv-2604-20052: Huang offers Annealed Langevin Monte Carlo for Flow ODE Sampling, a method for sampling unnormalized, multimodal distributions that trouble standard Markov chain Monte Carlo. A probability-flow ODE carries a standard Gaussian start at time zero to the target at time one. An annealed chain moves through intermediate stages, and Jarzynski weights yield a low-variance speed estimate. Theory gives an error bound shrinking as sample count grows, and tests on Gaussian mixes and a 64-dimensional Allen-Cahn system beat direct Monte Carlo and Hamiltonian Monte Carlo methods.
arxiv-2604-20152: Ashraf and three colleagues study particle output in neon-neon collisions at 5.36 TeV with the AMPT string-melting model. With spherical and deformed neon-20 nuclei, they track densities, identified yields, momentum spectra, mean momentum, and ratios against multiplicity and centrality. All observables follow usual trends, including smooth scaling with event size, mass order, and radial flow with quark coalescence. Deformation effects stay small, usually 2 to 6 percent and slightly stronger at the edges, so dynamics track system density rather than initial geometry.
arxiv-2604-20252: Pelttari, Küçükçifçi, and Yazıcı build globally simple integer Heffter arrays for an open case. A Heffter array fills part of a grid with distinct nonzero entries so rows and columns sum to zero, with global simplicity meaning partial sums stay distinct. Earlier work settled several classes, but k with remainder one on division by four above ten stayed open. The authors construct such arrays for k leaving remainder one on division by four with n leaving remainder zero or three, yielding orthogonal cyclic complete graph decompositions.
arxiv-2604-20352: Staritsin studies spin-up of the mass-gaining star in a close binary during Hertzsprung gap mass transfer, with mass leaking from the system. Spin gained hinges on how much mass the star adds, tested from 5 percent to 100 percent. Where the gainer ends at 16 solar masses, typical for early Be stars, spin moves inside the star via meridional circulation and shear turbulence. If accreted mass tops 30 percent, the gainer spins like an early Be star, regardless of prior spin, boundary-layer input, disk speed below Keplerian, or turbulence strength.
arxiv-2604-20552: Westrich and three colleagues generalize polytropic stellar wind models beyond the case of localized heating. Polytropic models describe the energy balance of expanding plasma without specifying heat conduction or wave heating. Earlier studies covered only adiabatic expansion of wind streams outside the heating region. Their study adds non-adiabatic behavior, with energy in a plausible range against flare energies and low against the gravitational energy of plasma. The solutions may interest stellar and solar wind work, given Parker Solar Probe observations of wind streams and acoustic waves near the Sun.
arxiv-2604-20752: Bujtas, Dettlaff, Furmanczyk, and Laskowska introduce majority C-coloring, in which each vertex matches the color of at least half of its neighbors. The maximum usable number of colors is called the majority C-chromatic number. For the k-th power of a path and a cycle, it equals floor of n over k-plus-1. The number is not monotone under edge deletion. Deciding whether the number is at least k is NP-complete for every fixed k of at least 2. A linear-time algorithm determines it for a tree.
arxiv-2604-21052: Liqi Jing and five colleagues turn image style transfer into a step-by-step prediction task, breaking pictures into layered codes and letting a transformer rebuild them under style and content guidance. A blending control balances texture against structure at each layer, and two training rounds, including reward-based fine-tuning, sharpen the match. Across three tests the system beat a standard baseline, holding scene structure best in landscapes and buildings.
arxiv-2604-21152: Irti Haq and Belén Saldías test whether language-model bias follows a stated identity or the dialect a user writes in, gathering over 24,000 replies from two open models. Stating a Black identity triggers strict safety filters with more refusals, while dialect cues slip past them, cutting refusals to near zero in a dialect jailbreak. The trade-off is raw, less sanitized answers, exposing safety tools tuned to keywords rather than real speech.
arxiv-2604-21252: Pedro Seber and Richard Braatz extend the LCEN algorithm, previously limited to regression, to classification while keeping its interpretability. On four binary and multiclass datasets, LCEN beats most of ten rival model types on macro F1 and Matthews correlation, while dropping an average of 56 percent of input features. Features LCEN selects also lift other models when retrained on them. A weighted focal differentiable MCC loss trained on the same data wins throughout, scoring 4.9 percent higher on macro F1 than weighted cross-entropy.
arxiv-2604-21352: Hagai Astrin and three colleagues build CARE, a response engine that helps counselors support people online in Hebrew and Arabic, where mental-health AI support remains thin. Tuned on curated sets of real crisis chats rated highly effective by professionals, the models learn patterns behind successful de-escalation. Training on full chat histories preserves evolving emotional context and dialogue structure. In tests, CARE aligns more closely with gold-standard counselor replies, semantically and strategically, than non-specialized models.
arxiv-2604-21552: Sara Koljančić and Polona Oblak study the non-symmetric Strong Spectral Property, linking digraphs with zero-nonzero matrix patterns and asking when they require or allow it, avoiding per-matrix checks. A new combinatorial method spots several patterns requiring the property. Loop assignments in double paths matter, and an open question on irreducible tridiagonal patterns gets a negative answer. They ask whether the minimum arc count in a directed graph on n vertices requiring it equals twice n minus one, confirming it for several families.
arxiv-2604-22852: Qiu and four colleagues propose SwarmDrive, in which nearby self-driving vehicles run small local language models. The vehicles share compact intent summaries only when uncertain, fusing them through event-triggered consensus instead of relying on cloud inference. In an occluded-intersection study, the 6G variant raises success to about 94 percent while cutting latency to about 151 milliseconds from a 510 millisecond cloud reference. Gains hold across robustness checks, though more vehicles raise communication overhead and packet loss. The authors stress this is not deployment-grade validation of a real 6G stack.
arxiv-2604-23052: Suchandra and Raayai-Ardakani study how formation angle affects drag in five-member V-formations, using non-lifting cylinders to isolate flow effects from lift. Time-resolved particle image velocimetry captures the velocity field around and between members. Drag reduction varies with angle, peaking near 80 percent for interior members of the tightest formation. All members gain some reduction up to about 50 degrees; beyond that, only the leading member shows observable reduction.
arxiv-2604-23352: Sun and four colleagues study model chains from cotorsion pairs in extriangulated categories. Starting from a hereditary Hovey triple, they build further triples with matching homotopy categories under fullness rules, refining earlier results. For objects of finite Gorenstein injective size over a class of E-triangles, they obtain a chain of model structures triangulated matching a common stable category. This repeats known results for Gorenstein injective modules and yields new cases in the derived category for cohomological ghost triangles.
arxiv-2604-23652: Huang, Lei, and Zhou solve the Cauchy problem for the 2D and 3D compressible Navier-Stokes-Korteweg system with data of any size. This extends large-data theory from the torus case, just solved, to whole space. Density totals may diverge there, posing fresh hurdles. A refined cutoff analysis plus a new tweaked Nash-Moser scheme beats them. The result assumes a friction law and a broad Bohm rule.
arxiv-2604-23752: Edmonds argues that two puzzles of the quiet-Sun corona, a stable disagreement between electron-temperature diagnostics and the failure of local heat-flow closure, are one and the same relative entropy. By a generalised Pythagorean identity for Bregman divergences, the entropy of the observed electron distribution splits cleanly, with no cross-term, into a closure deficit and a diagnostic gap. Any mechanism setting the distribution's shape must act on its suprathermal tail, non-locally.
arxiv-2604-23952: Giorgini offers a data-driven way to calibrate stochastic reduced models, the compact models used to stand in for complex systems. Standard methods lean on short trajectory steps, state partitions, or repeated simulation, all of which strain in high dimensions or with uneven sampling. His method links model drift and diffusion to the conditional score of the transition density, fitting both from lagged pairs alone. Tests on three systems of rising complexity preserve long-run statistics while matching short-lag dynamics.
arxiv-2604-24052: Jung and Kim propose QEVA, a metric that grades video summaries against the source video itself, with no human-written reference needed. It turns the summary into questions answered from multiple modes, scoring coverage, factuality, and chronology. A new benchmark of 800 summaries from 200 videos backs the approach, and QEVA tracks human judgment more closely than prior metrics on standard correlation measures.
arxiv-2604-24152: Fatehi and six colleagues simulate resonant Higgs bosons in electron-positron collisions at FCC-ee to constrain the electron Yukawa coupling. The signal, Higgs decay to W pairs in lepton-plus-jets final states, is separated from background with a boosted decision tree over kinematic and shape variables. With a narrowed energy spread and 10 inverse attobarns of data, the analysis reaches a combined significance of 2.0 standard deviations, giving the tightest simulation-based limit on the coupling to date.
arxiv-2604-24252: Claret and colleagues describe SVOM ground computing and user support at the French Science Center. The Sino-French mission for gamma-ray bursts and transients began operations in 2025 with three programs: the Core Program, the General Program, and Targets of Opportunity. The latter two are open to outside researchers with a mission co-investigator. Swift-style roles include Burst Advocates validating triggers and coordinating follow-up, and Instrument Scientists calibrating and validating data. The SVOM portal gives schedules, data, and tools, and the paper guides newcomers through Core Program operations.
arxiv-2604-24352: Alvarez-Merino and eight colleagues test multi-connectivity plans for reliable low-latency 5G uplinks in rural areas. Carrier 5G often serves downlinks well, but rural uplinks suffer radio limits and power-control rules. The team tracks uplink and downlink latency, packet loss, and radio signs across two nets. Latency and uptime cannot be read from signal bars alone, since power-limited uplinks and shared faults shape results. A PAAF system turns backup on as needed, and partial copying nears full multi-connectivity uptime with less copying overhead.
arxiv-2604-24752: Ramburuth-Hurt, De Cia, Krogager, Ledoux and Fox study parsec-scale interstellar dust clouds in the Milky Way's neutral medium, via dust depletion and dust extinction. They examine metal and dust distribution near the Sun and its Local Bubble links. Depletion data for gas clouds toward bright O and B stars within about 1 kiloparsec of the Sun combine with 3D extinction maps out to 1.25 kiloparsecs. Stronger extinction peaks match stronger depletion components to locate clouds in space, with chemically distinct clouds at least about 100 parsecs apart.
arxiv-2604-25052: Asano revisits the path-integral form of perturbative strings to address the IKKT matrix model. The paper reviews recent progress on the world-sheet integral, especially in Minkowski form. It derives a Minkowskian Nambu-Goto path integral matching Polyakov's Euclidean one for critical closed string theory. It shows matches among Nambu-Goto, Schild and Polyakov forms in both signatures. It also shows stringy causality shown in the path integral at string perturbation level. Matrix methods then yield a Minkowskian NBI-type IKKT model.
arxiv-2604-25152: Li and seven colleagues present MGTEVAL, a platform for systematic evaluation of machine-generated text detectors. Current evaluations scatter across data sets, preprocessing, attacks and metrics, so results are hard to compare or reproduce. MGTEVAL splits the work into data set building, attack, detector training and evaluation. It builds custom benchmarks with configurable language models, applies 12 text attacks to test sets and reports effectiveness, robustness and efficiency via command-line and web interfaces.
arxiv-2604-25252: Wang and three colleagues introduce a platform SMART trial, joining platform trials and sequential multiple assignment randomized trials so new treatments can join mid-trial. Dynamic treatment regimes are decision-rule sequences guiding choices as disease status evolves. Sequential trials are the gold standard for such regimes but take longer than single-stage trials, and new treatments may appear mid-trial. The authors also propose Bayesian integration G-formula estimators for non-concurrent cases, tested in simulations and shown on the S. aureus Network Adaptive Platform trial.
arxiv-2604-25452: Hamdi and five colleagues benchmark classic machine learning against BiLSTM with Attention for Indonesian product review sentiment. The set holds 19,728 reviews, split evenly between positive and negative. For classic learning, Logistic Regression, Support Vector Machine, and LightGBM were tried with 10-fold cross-checks, with Logistic Regression best at 97.26 percent accuracy and the same F1-score. The BiLSTM with Attention model, on 3,946 held-out test reviews, scored a touch lower on both measures. Classic learning thus rivals, and slightly beats, deeper sequential models, while running cheaper.
arxiv-2604-25652: The Euclid team analyses asteroid rotation periods from the Euclid Ecliptic Survey, run in late December 2023. The survey yields over 23,000 appearances of 2,321 known asteroids, which appear as streaks. Only 7 percent had published periods, so the team estimates spin periods from streak data. Validation against 48 published periods finds 44 percent within 1 percent and 98 percent within 15 percent. The team reports 889 high-quality periods, including 16 candidate super-fast rotators below the spin barrier of 2.2 hours and first-ever periods for 93 percent of the objects.
arxiv-2604-25952: Garg tabulates every P-position in 4-by-n Chomp for n up to 3000, over 961 million positions, with a new shadow-array sieve. Three structural findings follow. First, Unique Extension: any row-length triple admits at most one fourth value giving a P-position. Second, P-positions split persistently into HIGH and LOW families with a clean gap. That split exposes the conjectured global limit as a mixture artifact. Third, inside each family the larger row ratios obey an exact quadratic relation, with numeric evidence for specific family limits.
arxiv-2604-26052: Hu, Wei, and Atluri pair prompt risk with response risk for language model safety. In four harm categories, 61 percent of replies reduce harm, 36 percent hold level, and 3 percent escalate. Escalation splits into benign prompts triggering harmful detail and on-task answers of higher severity. Sexual content shows the highest harm persistence, from same-level compliance, not benign-input drift. Compliance escalations stay highly relevant; safe replies are generic low-relevance refusals. A public check over 600 prompts and six models reproduces two directional signals.
arxiv-2604-26252: Ye and five colleagues introduced OmniTrend, a tool that predicts how popular a social-media post will be. It keeps two parts apart: the pull of the post itself, and how far the platform spreads it. One part reads sights, sounds, and words to gauge the post's own appeal, while the other weighs post time, author habits, trends, and nearby posts to gauge spread. Keeping the two parts apart shows what each one adds and helps the tool move across image and video sites.
arxiv-2604-26352: Song, Lee, and Seo asked how well vision-language models predict where people look on screens. Using eye-tracking data for 1,980 interface screenshots across web, desktop, mobile, and poster layouts, they ran nine leading models through a zero-shot gaze-point pipeline. Model gaze maps matched human gaze only moderately, with fit varying by interface type and improving as viewing time grew. The pattern suggests models capture roaming exploration better than first fixations.
arxiv-2604-26552: Zhang and three colleagues studied cooperative OFDM sensing-and-communication networks, where several base stations sense jointly. Two fusion designs were weighed: signal-level fusion, which forwards raw echoes to a center, and parameter-level fusion, which reports only local delay and Doppler estimates with uncertainties. For signal fusion they derived a Cramér-Rao bound on joint position and velocity; for parameter fusion they built a two-stage bound-like metric. Joint resource-element selection and power allocation, solved by alternating optimization, suppressed ambiguity sidelobes and beat baselines.
arxiv-2604-26652: Svarc asks whether a bunching of poles noted by Hoehler in pion-nucleon scattering could come from the extraction method itself. Exact unitarity keeps angular momenta separate, but practical pole extraction from two-way data forces truncation of the partial-wave series. A mixing effect from truncation, shown in an earlier paper, lets fitted coefficients inherit overlapping pole content. The result offers a plausible partial explanation for Hoehler-type bunching without invoking true mixing between angular momenta.
arxiv-2604-26852: Casaburi and Vivo study the top eigenvalue and eigenvector of large Euclidean random matrices, whose entries link through the geometry of scattered points. With a replica-based method, they shrink the large-size limit to a Fredholm operator problem set by the kernel and point spread. For the quadratic distance kernel the problem drops to a finite set of self-consistent equations. That gives an explicit mean top value from low-order moments and an analytic density for the top vector's parts. Broad simulations back the predictions.
arxiv-2604-26952: Koliogiannis and Paar quantify how current nuclear mass models shape the outer crust of neutron stars, near the minimum-mass limit. They build four outer-crust equations of state from relativistic energy-density functionals and machine-learning mass tables, finding equilibrium compositions by minimizing Gibbs free energy per nucleon. Different mass inputs shift the nuclide sequence, the last bound nuclei, and the neutron-drip density. Yet bulk thermodynamic properties and minimum-mass star configurations stay closely aligned, making the crust equations a reliable input for stellar models.
arxiv-2604-27052: Dogra posits an outline for a unified theory of learning, optimization, and modeling, reading learning broadly. He views learning as a linked process on several levels: problem setup, method choice, and study of their interplay via imposed dynamics. He proposes a precise, flexible definition for solvable problems, then defines parameter methods for learning solutions. His goal is a universal convergence theorem, stating when solvable problems become amenable to chosen methods. The constructions reduce learning to few ideas and tools, adapted from dynamical systems, geometry, and physics.
arxiv-2604-27152: DeGoede and Haji build one joint design framework for wave-driven desalination. It pairs wave energy converters with seawater reverse osmosis to ease freshwater scarcity. High cost blocks wide use, so their plan joins models of wave motion, power transfer, osmosis limits, and costs in one optimization. Tuning those coupled parts together cuts the levelized cost of water sharply. Joint design thus beats tuning each part alone.
arxiv-2604-27752: Altmann and three colleagues study string closepacking in proton-proton collisions, where crossing strings create a background field raising real string tension. Stronger tension reduces strange loss, lifting strange hadron output, which the Monash-tuned Lund String Model does not describe. The model adds popcorn destructive interference, cutting baryon output, and strange junctions, boosting strange output in the baryon sector. Tuned to LHC data with Trieste tunes, the closepacking model matches many measured ratios broadly, beating older PYTHIA models without extra proton yields.
arxiv-2604-27952: Hou and colleagues tackle image compression plus wireless sending as one joint problem instead of treating them separately. Their training-free Diffusion-OAMP method feeds a pretrained diffusion model into an orthogonal approximate message passing scheme, matching noise levels between its linear and nonlinear stages. Across varied compression and noise settings it beats classic methods in their tests.
arxiv-2604-28052: Britto, Oliveira and Kleinebrahm model how households spend, invest and take up energy-saving tech when the future is unsure, all in one setup. They rework rebound and backfire effects, fold welfare effects into best subsidy design, and show take-up thresholds hinge on wealth, a new link from finances to tech choices. Take-up mostly lifts welfare, and a German single-family home case plus number-crunching show subsidies steering total energy use well.
arxiv-2605-00052:
Sungjun Cho studies how to train three-dimensional Gaussian splatting on hybrid captures, scenes shot from very different distances such as drone and ground views. The standard recipe, one rendered view per optimizer step, under-fits the minority viewpoint regime on five benchmarks. Cho compares compute-matched fixes, from longer training and gradient corrections to surgery on conflicting gradients, and finds the simplest structural change wins.

Rendering two views per step closes the gap, and the pairing rule, whether geometry-based, random, or driven by loss disparity, makes no difference beyond seed noise. His variance-decomposition framework explains why: between-regime gradient variance is small next to within-regime variance, so halving variance by accumulation dominates. The negative results are reported plainly, and the two-view lever transfers to two other splatting backbones.
arxiv-2605-00252:
George K. Leontaris and George Prampromis explore primordial black holes as dark matter candidates inside a theory with two extra dimensions. In their six-dimensional setting, the basic energy scale sits near ten trillion electron volts, within reach of future experiments. They analyze small black holes that carry charge and spin.

Under ordinary Hawking evaporation, only black holes heavier than a hundred million grams survive to today, though near-extremal ones live longer. Under the memory burden scenario, where evaporation is heavily suppressed, even sub-gram black holes can survive. The authors argue such objects could appear at a future collider as events with many particles and thermal energy patterns. Their mass pattern also lines up suggestively with the known neutrino mass scale.
arxiv-2605-00352:
Arpit Thool and Chris Brown report from inside an organization that wove log-based security analytics into its Agile software workflow. Log data can flag account takeovers and abuse, but security work often clashes with fast weekly delivery cycles. Real-world case studies of such integrations are scarce, which is the gap this experience report fills.

A cross-functional team of eight, including one author, spent weekly cycles building a proof-of-concept system nicknamed the Red Flag Project. It alerts stakeholders when accounts show suspicious activity patterns. Through semi-structured interviews, the authors studied how developers perceived the system: their willingness to adopt it, the friction it caused, and its effect on daily work and on security awareness. They distill lessons and best practices for teams attempting the same embedding.
arxiv-2605-00452:
Tishkov Vladislav presents an ambitious mathematical construction linking finite graphs to string theory. From any finite graph he builds a compact Riemann surface, a spectral curve, whose period matrix encodes the graph's coarse spectral information. As graph sequences refine toward a smooth curved space, he argues these curves converge to the classical curves attached to that space.

The work connects the construction to topological recursion and matrix models. It introduces a spectral memory field on the curve. It also builds quantum scattering operators whose unitarity is tied to a positivity condition on that field. In its boldest application, the framework is applied to the chaotic regime near spacelike singularities in general relativity. There the author argues the singularity is replaced by an infinite chain of rational curves. These are the paper's presented claims, offered as rigorous foundations for discrete approaches to quantum gravity.
arxiv-2605-00652:
Andreas Dombos, Junyang Gou, and Benedikt Soja turn monthly satellite gravity maps into daily ones without washing out their detail. The GRACE missions weigh Earth's water storage monthly, a rhythm too slow for fast hydrological events. Existing daily products sacrifice spatial resolution to smoothing, since each day's satellite ground tracks are sparse. Their framework, D-SHIFT, learns to transfer the sharp spatial information of monthly products into daily fields.

A generative adversarial network is trained in the monthly domain: blurred daily-style inputs and auxiliary features go in, and the official monthly mascon products are the target. The trained model then upgrades real daily solutions the same way. Monthly validation matched the official products closely, with global errors of a few centimeters of water. Daily fields stayed coherent and sharpened basin trends. In Greenland it recovered coastal mass-loss patterns, with a basin trend close to the reference value.
arxiv-2605-00952:
Stavros Mouslopoulos asks which coherence actually decoheres in a symmetry-broken collective spin system, where the answer depends on the basis chosen. In the ordered phase, localized pointer states and energy eigenstates give Lindblad dephasing rates that differ by a factor approaching two for large systems, and higher near the quantum-critical crossover. The discrepancy has a single algebraic origin in parity.

Parity forces a key expectation value to vanish exactly in the energy basis, removing a cross-term that doubles the localized-state rate. Two distinct protection factors are identified and quantified. In the thermodynamic limit the secular approximation fails, the doublet degenerates, and both rates converge. Results are demonstrated in the Lipkin-Meshkov-Glick model by exact diagonalisation.
arxiv-2605-01552:
Bao-Long Tran, Cuong Le, Fredrik Viksten, and Per-Erik Forssén recover camera motion from a single blurred photo. Robots and headsets need relative pose between views, usually read from matched points across sharp frames; fast motion smears one frame so badly that the standard geometry tools fail.

Their framework, GeoBlur, reads the smear itself as evidence. It first predicts matching points between two instants inside the exposure window. Then it solves for the fundamental matrix that fits a single frame under a time-direction ambiguity. That ambiguity leaves the matrix fixed only up to transposition. On synthetic and hybrid benchmarks the method improves over prior work, and it stays competitive on real blur data. A further test uses the recovered geometry for motion segmentation from one frame, a task that normally demands a clean video.
arxiv-2605-01752:
